source_acquisition.search_note: The local inventory row still says no_public_source_found and has no compact visual-source directory. I checked the paper PDF links, OpenReview/project URLs, local inventory, a unicli search, agent-reach doctor, gh auth and GitHub repository trees. The official project-page repository contains exact rendered assets for Figures 4 and 19; the linked VJA repository contains exact rendered assets for Figures 1–3 plus defense code. It does not contain the complete paper plotting/table source for Figures 5–18 or Tables 1–8, so those properties remain rendered estimates rather than source-exact claims. The VJA README also says full evaluation code is not yet released.

paper_style.palette_strategy: The paper uses pastel/cyan composites for benchmark and qualitative objects; blue/green for TJA/VJA; ordered pastel risk-level bars; blue/green reasoning bars; red default/reference and red/green sensitivity text; and a separate neutral/cyan data-format style. Text labels, spatial grouping, direct values and row/column identity provide partial redundancy, but small qualitative panels and red/green encodings are not grayscale/color-vision robust.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The verified PDF combines PDF text/math/table objects with embedded raster composites. Source-exact PNG assets are visible for Figures 1–4 and 19; chart-like Figures 5, 7 and 14–17 appear as mixed or embedded rendered objects, while qualitative grids/montages are raster-heavy. All 27 physical pages were rendered at 200 dpi to /tmp/icml132_render200/page-01.png through page-27.png; contact sheets and object pages were inspected, including references and appendix pages.
paper_style.style_consistency: The ICML two-column article shell, caption placement, Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern math table typography and restrained horizontal rules are consistent. Figure assets introduce Arial/Impact/monospace/handwritten-like raster lettering, and the project-page graphics use a brighter web palette; structural vocabulary and recurring category/model labels are more consistent than font family. The principal cross-object omissions are uncertainty definitions, denominators, model-panel mapping and exact sample-selection rules.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Comparison between our Vision-Centric Jailbreak Attack (VJA) and conventional Text-Centric Jailbreak Attacks. Top: Attack scheme comparison; Bottom: Performance comparison on a subset of IESBench, VJA achieves significantly higher attack success rates across four commercial models.

color.semantic_mapping: Figure 1 and Table 2 use blue for TJA and green/gray for VJA; labels and direct ASR/HS/EV/HRR values repeat the comparison.

encodings.x: bottom panel: four commercial models as categorical groups
encodings.color: TJA blue versus VJA green; top panel uses labeled attack paths rather than a numeric color scale
encodings.shape: image/text callout cards and grouped bars
encodings.line: top arrows show attack flow; bottom has no trend line
encodings.facet: top attack-scheme comparison and bottom performance comparison
encodings.text: TJA, VJA, Input Image, Input Text, Harmfulness Score, model names, ASR values and deltas

figures.data_and_statistics: Top is a visual attack-scheme comparison; bottom is a four-model grouped bar chart. PDF labels show TJA/VJA ASR values 48.8/84.4, 46.8/71.7, 88.8/96.1, and 93.2/93.7 with corresponding deltas +35.6, +24.9, +7.3, +0.5; no uncertainty or denominator is printed in the figure.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction claim that visual-only prompts evade text-centric defenses → Figure 1 establishes the attack interface and headline ASR contrast → Table 1 and Figure 5 expand to all 1054 IESBench samples and four metrics.
design_strengths: The upper/lower split makes the conceptual mechanism and quantitative headline scannable.
Direct numbers and delta callouts reduce dependence on bar-height estimation.
The same TJA/VJA vocabulary is reused in Table 2 and the analytic comparison.
design_weaknesses: The upper image montage and lower bar chart use unrelated visual grammars in one object.
Caption says “significantly higher” but gives no statistical or repeated-run definition; the figure has no uncertainty encoding.
The source raster warning says “5x Harmfulness Score” while the lower chart reports ASR, creating a possible metric-label mismatch; small callout text is hard to read when reduced.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a conceptual before/after attack panel with a compact grouped-bar headline; repeat the condition in labels, colors, and direct deltas, and make the metric and statistical basis explicit.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: VJA performance on our constructed IESBench. The most risky and safest category for each model are marked by red and blue separately. Metric arrows and ALL column make direction and aggregate target explicit.
Red/blue risk highlights and rank icons speed safety-oriented scanning.
design_weaknesses: Eighteen columns and 32 metric rows are extremely dense at page width.
Caption says “BAGEL, Qwen-Local” while the visible model rows include BAGEL, Flux2.0[dev], Qwen-Image-Edit* local and Qwen-Image-Edit-Safe Ours; the caption/header naming is inconsistent.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figures 1–4 move from the VJA/TJA threat interface to benchmark statistics, defense mechanism and curation pipeline. Table 1 and Figure 5 then establish the main category/risk-level comparison; Figure 6 and Table 2 pair a qualitative case with TJA/VJA deltas; Figure 7 and Table 3 isolate reasoning and judge effects. Appendix Table 4/Figure 8 fix the taxonomy and exemplars, Figures 9–12 provide qualitative outputs and failures, Figures 13–15 test visual-prompt sensitivity, Figures 16–17 expose judge-dependent HS distributions, Tables 5–7 cover complexity/agreement/generalization, Figure 18 positions the benchmark against prior work, and Figure 19 fixes the file format.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions consistently begin with a descriptive title and then identify the object’s setup or comparison. Figures 1, 6 and Table 1 make directional claims or rankings; most other captions are descriptive. Captions often omit denominator, model-panel mapping, exact aggregation and uncertainty definitions. Captions for Figures 9/10, Figure 17 and Table 1 contain naming/count ambiguities that are visible only when the rendered object is compared with the PDF text.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables use compact single-level headers, upward/downward metric arrows, model/category columns and minimal/booktabs-like horizontal rules. Table 1 adds model/metric hierarchy and cell color/ranking glyphs; Tables 2–3 use paired rows or judge rows; Appendix Tables 4–8 switch to taxonomy, cost, agreement, transfer and model metadata. Header direction is useful, but the switch from ↑ metrics in the main table to ↓ metrics in Table 7 needs a caption-level reminder.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The visual-only attack interface in Figure 1 and the benchmark vocabulary in Figures 2/4 are instantiated by Table 1/Figure 5. Figure 3’s safety trigger maps to Figure 7’s reasoning ablation, Table 5’s overhead and Table 7’s transfer. Figure 6/Table 2 quantify the TJA/VJA contrast introduced in Figure 1, while Table 3 and Figures 16–17 test whether judge choice changes the evidence. Figures 13–15 connect controlled prompt alterations to robustness outcomes.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Table 1/Figure 5 summarize all categories and risk levels; Appendix Table 4/Figure 8 provide definitions and exemplars, Figures 9–10 provide output-level cases, and Figures 16–17 provide judge distributions. Main Figure 3 and Figure 7 are extended by Table 5, Table 7 and Table 6. Figure 4’s curation path is completed by Figure 19’s storage format and Table 8’s evaluated roster.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF tables and captions use embedded Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern-style objects at approximately 7–9 pt; figure labels are commonly approximately 4.5–8 pt after embedding. Exact linked PNG assets carry their own raster typography and cannot establish a paper-wide font rule. The result is a stable article shell with mixed graphic lettering and occasional monospace/code styling.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/green remains the main TJA/VJA and reasoning contrast; risk-level bars use ordered pastel colors; red is reused for unsafe/default/positive emphasis and blue/green for safe/negative or open-model cues. Labels, direct values, row/column position and arrows add redundancy, but red/green sensitivity text, tiny pastel qualitative panels and overlapping commercial/open palettes weaken grayscale and color-vision robustness.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1’s conceptual attack comparison plus direct-delta grouped bars gives a compact threat-to-headline bridge; a paired table then carries the full metric detail.
Figure 2/4/8/19 form a reusable benchmark chain: scale cards and examples, curation provenance, one exemplar per taxonomy class, and machine-readable storage format.
A fixed model/category matrix with direct HS/Denied labels (Figures 9–10) complements aggregate metric tables without pretending qualitative cases are prevalence estimates.
Figures 13–15 connect one-factor visual perturbation examples, default-relative influence summaries and box/dot distributions to make robustness claims interpretable.
Figures 16–17 reuse identical discrete-score small multiples under two judges, allowing judge dependence to be visually compared and then quantified in Tables 3/6.
highest_value_objects: Table 1: the primary category-by-metric safety decision surface across 1054 IESBench images and eight model configurations.
Figure 1: the clearest high-level explanation of why VJA is different from TJA and where the headline ASR contrast comes from.
Figure 4: the strongest dataset-reproducibility object because it combines risk taxonomy with collection, quality control, prompting and evaluation steps.
Figures 16–17: matched judge-distribution panels that expose the dependence of HS evidence on evaluator choice.
Figure 19 plus Table 8: compact reproduction anchors for data layout and evaluated model roster.
failure_patterns: Captions frequently show exact-looking values without defining denominator, replicate aggregation or uncertainty; Figure 7 error caps and Table 3 HS± are especially underspecified.
Dense composites, qualitative grids and small multiples rely on tiny labels, pastel/red-green color and long model names; reduction and grayscale materially weaken inspection.
Figure 9’s caption/page row-range continuity, Figure 17’s eight-versus-nine model count and Table 1’s model-name wording create avoidable audit ambiguity.
Table 5 omits runtime units and Figure 14 omits the formal definition of maximum/extreme influence, limiting direct reproducibility of efficiency/robustness claims.

Qualitative failure and benchmark-comparison objects are useful mechanisms/examples but provide no sample-selection rule or prevalence, so they cannot independently support aggregate safety conclusions.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a recurring VJA/TJA, I1–I15, risk-level and judge vocabulary to move from threat interface and dataset construction through category metrics, paired qualitative cases, defense/robustness ablations, judge distributions and file-format/model-roster details, with strong structural reuse but incomplete uncertainty and provenance definitions.
